title: Hightide Labs Renewal + APAC Private Pilot Sync
summary: Quarterly renewal checkpoint focusing on a one-year contract extension with a capacity bump, onboarding APAC private deployment pilot, and security/compliance items. Redwood team clarified Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, discussed latency targets and cost expectations, and agreed on a pilot plan and next milestones.
topics: contract extension timeline and proposed term
capacity bump: estimated GPU hours and burst profile
APAC private pilot (VPC/on-prem options) and networking requirements
SLA and security: SOC2, audit logs, KMS/HSM integration
benchmarks: latency targets, throughput and quantization recommendations
pricing implications and discounts for reserved capacity
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2027-11-07 09:34 PT
Duration: 56 minutes
Recorded by Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Desai (Redwood SE); Maya Patel (Hightide, Dir MLOps); Liam O'Connor (VP Eng); Sofia Reyes (Security Lead)

Summary (auto): Renewal check-in to confirm capacity bump and pilot timeline for APAC Private deployment. Action: send pricing, schedule pilot kickoff, share security pack.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, can you all hear me okay?
[00:04] Maya Patel: Yep, sounds good. We got a bit of overlap with the engineering stand, but fine.
[00:12] Alex Chen: Great. Today's agenda: contract term extension, capacity uplift for Q1, and the APAC private pilot details you asked for. Priya will walk the technical plan.
[00:24] Priya Desai: Hi all. I'll start with the deployment options. We have the Redwood Dedicated plan — reserved GPU pools — which gives predictable throughput. The Private option is where we provision a private control plane into your V-P-C or an on‑prem package if you need air-gap. For APAC we can do a regional private edge or a hybrid: control plane in our region, data plane in your VPC.
[00:46] Liam O'Connor: For latency we need sub‑120ms p99 for our customer-facing chat endpoints in APAC. Is that achievable with the private pilot?
[00:55] Priya Desai: Yes, with local APAC GPUs and optimized kernels we can hit ~90–110ms p99 on the 7B class models given your 256 token windows. But two caveats: 1) K-V cache warmup matters — if you have cold starts there's a penalty, and 2) model variant and quantization change latency/cost.
[01:18] Maya Patel: When you say quantization change, are you recommending 4-bit? We ran into hallucination increases last time when we cranked quant.
[01:25] Priya Desai: We usually recommend mixed strategy: int8 for generation paths where quality is tolerant, and per-route profiling. Redwood Optimize can propose per-route quant settings based on evals you upload. Also we can do a short A/B with your prompts during the pilot.
[01:41] Sofia Reyes: From security side, we need KMS integration and proof of HSM-based key separation. Also SOC 2 Type II report and audit logs exported to our SIEM.
[01:51] Alex Chen: Absolutely. We'll share the security pack: SOC2 docs, encryption-at-rest details, and the KMS/HSM integration guide. For audit logs, Redwood Console can stream logs; we have an S3 or SIEM connector.
[02:06] Sofia Reyes: And SSO — SAML with SCIM provisioning for RBAC.
[02:10] Alex Chen: Yep, SAML + SCIM supported. We'll include a sample SAML metadata file.
[02:16] Liam O'Connor: Pricing — if we go with a 12‑month extension and add APAC private pilot, what's the expected delta? We are looking at a 30–40% uplift in peak GPU hours.
[02:26] Alex Chen: Ballpark: dedicated reserved capacity with a committed monthly usage will net you a discount versus on-demand. For a 30–40% capacity bump we can propose a two‑tier pricing: base reserved plus burst capacity at a defined uplift rate. I'll send a spreadsheet.
[02:40] Maya Patel: We have procurement windows — we need signed PO by Dec 15 to align with our Q1 budget. Can Redwood commit to an implementation date?
[02:48] Priya Desai: For APAC private pilot, typical lead time is 4–6 weeks from contract signature for provisioning and network peering tests, maybe faster if you provide the network details early.
[02:59] Maya Patel: 4–6 weeks is tight, but doable. We'll need a pilot plan that includes benchmarks and a rollback plan.
[03:06] Priya Desai: We'll draft a pilot runbook: topology, kv cache priming strategy, sample prompts, benchmark harness and acceptance criteria. We'll also include a canary traffic plan — start at 5% then ramp.
[03:19] Speaker 3: (muffled) can you say that again about the KV —
[03:22] Priya Desai: Sorry, I said KV cache priming — it's important for latency. If you pre-warm popular prefixes you avoid cold token cost.
[03:29] Liam O'Connor: About model fallbacks — if the APAC nodes run out of capacity, what's the fallback? Do calls route to hosted models in another region?
[03:36] Priya Desai: We can configure smart routing: by policy you can prefer private region, then fall back to our hosted API in the nearest region or a cheaper model variant. That is part of the resilience story.
[03:45] Maya Patel: Are there throughput SLOs during burst? We can't have degraded latency that impacts SLAs.
[03:51] Alex Chen: With Dedicated the SLA covers throughput and uptime; with Private pilot we'll define SLO targets and a support escalation path. For bursts we can set auto-burst to our nearby capacity but that would be billed differently.
[04:03] Sofia Reyes: For compliance, we need data residency guarantees for APAC customers. Can Redwood ensure logs and persisted tokens remain in-region?
[04:10] Priya Desai: Yes, in Private we can isolate logs and storage to your region. We'll list exact data flow in the pilot runbook.
[04:18] Liam O'Connor: One more: someone mentioned MajorCloudAI in a previous thread. How do we compare on latency/cost? They offered lower per‑token rates but no private control plane.
[04:27] Alex Chen: Competitor note: MajorCloudAI often undercuts on list price but lacks private deployment and full audit log exports; OpenStream has a strong edge in compression but not the same operational playbook. We'll include a short competitive slide.
[04:40] Maya Patel: Great. On the contract term — we're inclined to 12 months with an option to extend if pilot metrics look good. Any early termination provisions?
[04:48] Alex Chen: Standard 30‑day notice for downgrades, and we can include an early termination clause tied to missed SLOs for enterprise customers. Priya, anything on the migration effort if they choose to later move to Dedicated at scale?
[04:59] Priya Desai: Migration is pretty seamless — you can pin model versions and rollout policies. We'll do a canary cutover and the runtime handles KV cache and batching differences; there are operational runbooks.
[05:12] Sofia Reyes: For the pilot acceptance criteria can we set a p99 <= 120ms and <1% error rate on production-like traffic?
[05:19] Priya Desai: That sounds reasonable. We'll propose acceptance thresholds in the runbook and capture the exact test prompts.
[05:26] Liam O'Connor: Who's owning the pilot on Redwood?
[05:29] Alex Chen: Priya will be the technical lead and I'll coordinate commercial and timelines.
[05:33] Maya Patel: Ok. Quick note: our finance needs a single line item for invoicing — do you support consolidated billing across regions?
[05:40] Alex Chen: Yes, consolidated billing with regional tagging is doable. We'll provide a sample invoice template.
[05:45] Maya Patel: Awesome. Anything else?
[05:48] Alex Chen: Let's run through next steps.
[05:51] Priya Desai: I'll follow up with the pilot runbook and benchmark harness this week. Alex will send pricing and the contract amendment draft. Security pack goes to Sofia.
[06:00] Sofia Reyes: I'll review SOC2 and KMS integration, and ping infra for network peering details.
[06:06] Liam O'Connor: We'll gather the test prompt set and expected traffic patterns.
[06:10] Alex Chen: Cool. Thanks everyone. We'll target a pilot kickoff week of Dec 20 if contracts close by Dec 15.
[06:18] Maya Patel: Sounds good. Thanks.

Meeting end: 10:30 PT
